lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eCon el mismo esquelet:
"

With the same skeleton, the substituents determine the function: cholesterol has OH at C3, a C5=C6 double bond and an 8-carbon side chain at C17; testosterone has C3=O, C4=C5 and OH at C17; estradiol has an aromatic A ring (no C19) with a phenolic OH; progesterone has C3=O, C4=C5 and an acetyl group at C17. Compare the four.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eDos moléculas de farn:
"

Two molecules of farnesyl-PP join “tail to tail” to give squalene (C₃₀). Squalene monooxygenase forms the epoxide and a cyclization cascade (like those seen in electrophilic addition) closes four rings and generates lanosterol. In about 19 more steps 3 methyls are lost and cholesterol (C₂₇) is obtained. Move the control to see the folding.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa biosíntesis usa \u:
"

Biosynthesis uses isopentenyl pyrophosphate (IPP) and dimethylallyl pyrophosphate (DMAPP): one DMAPP + one IPP give geranyl-PP (C₁₀); another IPP, farnesyl-PP (C₁₅); another, geranylgeranyl-PP (C₂₀). The corresponding alcohols (geraniol, farnesol, geranylgeraniol) keep the pattern: each unit contributes a 4-C chain with a methyl on the third carbon.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLos \u003cb\u003eeste:
"

Steroids share the cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene nucleus: rings A, B, C (cyclohexane) and D (cyclopentane), numbered C1–C17. The methyls C18 (on C13) and C19 (on C10) usually point up (β). The ring fusions are trans, giving an almost flat, rigid skeleton that inserts between membrane lipids.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLos \u003cb\u003eterp:
"

Terpenes are natural products formed from isoprene (2-methylbuta-1,3-diene, C₅H₈) units joined “head to tail”. They are classified by the number of units: monoterpenes (2 units, C₁₀), sesquiterpenes (3, C₁₅), diterpenes (4, C₂₀), triterpenes (6, C₃₀) and tetraterpenes (8, C₄₀, carotenoids). Each color in the figure marks one unit.

"
